trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Going to (7,4,2) would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,2,1).
The line must go to (4,2,1): to (6,1,2) is number 18, which comes later; to (6,4,1) is number 4, which comes later.
Going to (4,1,2) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,4,1).
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (6,6,1): to (4,7,2) is number 8, which comes later.

Going to (7,6,2) would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going to (6,7,2) would strand number 4: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (6,4,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (7,4,2).
Going to (7,4,4), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (7,6,4). So the line goes to (7,6,2).
Going to (6,7,2) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,6,4).
Going to (7,4,4) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,6,6).
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (4,6,7) would force the line onto number 14 before its turn; going to (2,7,6) would leave number 7 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (4,7,4).
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going to (1,6,4) would force the line onto number 13 before its turn. So the line goes to (1,4,2).
Going to (1,4,4) would leave number 10 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (1,2,2).
Going to (2,1,2) would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (2,2,1).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,1,2).
Going to (4,1,2) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes to (2,1,4).
Number 11 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (1,4,4): to (1,2,6) is number 23, which comes later.
Going to (1,6,4) would force the line onto number 13 before its turn. So the line goes to (1,4,6).
Number 12 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (1,6,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,4).
Going to (4,4,7) would force the line onto number 21 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,6,7).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,4,7).
Going to (4,4,7) would force the line onto number 21 before its turn. So the line goes to (6,2,7).
Going to number 15, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 17. So the line goes to (6,1,6).
Going to (6,1,4) would force the line onto number 18 before its turn; going to (4,1,6) would cut off a group of 6 cells. So the line goes to (7,2,6).
Number 16 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Number 20 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (4,4,7): to (2,2,7) is number 22, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
